sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or give reasons).

questions.q: As a community health worker, you advise a young couple about safe motherhood. Choose two recommendations and give a reason for each: (i) Avoid pregnancy before 18 years and after 35 years. (ii) Plan frequent pregnancies to have more children early. (iii) Keep a gap of more than two years between two pregnancies. (iv) Medical check-ups during pregnancy are not essential.
questions.answer: (i) Avoid pregnancy before 18 and after 35: it is unsafe for the mother's and the child's health. (iii) Keep a gap of more than two years: the mother's body recovers and the child gets care.

questions.q: Identify the two correct steps to help a mentally retarded child. (i) Teach self-help skills (ii) Enrol them in a regular school (iii) Teach him braille and sign language (iv) Involve him in simple household tasks.
State whether True or False and justify. (a) Mentally retarded children should be involved in simple household tasks. (b) Body contact in crowded places may cause HIV transmission.
questions.answer: (a) True: it keeps them occupied and makes them independent. (b) False: HIV does not spread by casual contact.

questions.q: Match Column A with Column B. A: (a) Blind child (b) Deaf child. B: (i) Sign language and lip reading (ii) Braille and a stick (iii) Artificial limb.
Write the full form of AIDS and HIV.
questions.answer: AIDS: Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome. HIV: Human Immunodeficiency Virus.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Explain any two major physical disabilities in children and one problem faced by each.
questions.answer: Blindness: the child cannot read or find the way, so needs Braille and a stick. Deafness: the child cannot hear his own voice so cannot learn language.

or.q: Explain how education helps a girl child in becoming a better mother in the future.
or.answer: An educated girl can look after her children's studies and develop good habits and values. She understands their daily problems and gives meaningful solutions.

questions.q: Imagine you are a teacher and notice a child labourer in your locality. What steps would you take to help the child return to school?
questions.answer: I would meet the parents and explain the harm of child labour and the value of education. I would arrange non-formal education and ask the employer to free the child for school.

questions.q: Give three reasons why so much emphasis is being placed on educating girls.
questions.answer: It gives awareness and the ability to run the household efficiently. It gives financial independence and educated mothers raise better children.

questions.q: Mention three ways in which poverty leads to juvenile delinquency.
questions.answer: Poor children lack facilities and find stealing easy. Parents may encourage them to steal or beg, and lack of play and education leads them into bad company.

or.q: Which three precautions should be adopted at the time of delivery?
or.answer: A skilled person should be present at delivery and a hospital referral should be possible. The newborn must be kept clean, the cord tied and cut hygienically, and breast-feeding started early.

questions.q: Define juvenile delinquency. Mention two delinquent behaviours.
questions.answer: It is violation of law by young people (a boy below 16 and a girl below 18). Examples are stealing and violence.

questions.q: What is meant by child labour? State two causes.
questions.answer: It is work by children below 14 years to earn a living. Poverty and illiteracy of parents are causes.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: List various discriminations against the girl child.
questions.answer: (i) She is fed after the males and gets inadequate food, and is breast-fed for a shorter time. (ii) She is not taken to the doctor when sick, so many die in infancy. (iii) She is taken out of school early and made to do household chores.

questions.q: Suggest preventive measures for juvenile delinquency (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Remove poverty through loans and vocational training. (ii) Parents should spend time with children and inculcate good habits and values. (iii) Provide recreational facilities and remand homes for reform and vocational training.

questions.q: Explain the consequences of child labour (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Long hours in poor postures cause permanent disability. (ii) Unhygienic conditions cause infectious diseases. (iii) Missing school adds to illiteracy.

questions.q: Explain how mentally retarded children can be helped (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Never call them stupid; let them do things themselves. (ii) Teach self-help skills and involve them in simple household tasks. (iii) Enrol them in special schools for vocational training.

questions.q: List the modes of HIV transmission.
questions.answer: (i) Through infected blood and unsterilised needles, blades and instruments. (ii) From an infected mother to the child before or during birth and breast-feeding. (iii) Through unprotected sex with an infected partner.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Write a note on safe motherhood.
questions.answer: (i) Safe motherhood aims at reducing maternal mortality and morbidity. (ii) Avoid pregnancy before 18 and after 35–37 years. (iii) Plan the family with a gap of more than two years and two or three children. (iv) Use contraceptives: natural, mechanical (condom, Copper T), chemical or surgical. (v) Consult a qualified nurse or doctor in pregnancy and have a skilled person at delivery. (vi) Keep the newborn clean, tie the cord safely and start breast-feeding early.
